newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar near year low on regional woes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar near year low on regional woes.

text.p: The Singapore dollar looks set to see new year lows against the U.S. dollar after breaking through psychological support at 1.4500, dealers said on Thursday.
In early morning trade, the Singapore dollar touched 1.4535, the previous low it hit in March, they said.
"The Singapore dollar is falling in sympathy with the ringgit and the rupiah," said a dealer with a U.S. institution.
Dealers said some hedge funds were selling the Singapore dollar after stop-losses were triggered at above the 1.4500 level.
The Singapore dollar was expected to trade within a new range of 1.4480 and 1.4550 to the dollar, they said.
Dealers said one of the reasons for the slide in the local currency was also the noticeable absence from the market of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank.
"There were no signs of them in the market nor was there any talk of checking rates," said a dealer with a European bank.
"There is a likelihood MAS is allowing the Singapore dollar to ease along with the other currencies in the region to maintain its competitive edge," said another dealer.
